content.thinking:
I'm planning to write this file in one pass without typecheck feedback, so I want to keep the code simple and robust. I'm designing a standing female cyborg medic figure facing forward, roughly 1.75m tall, with a palette of cream armor, teal and coral accents, gold trim, dark panels, cyan glow details, and warm skin and hair tones.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: hips root, a spine chain running hips to chest to neck to head, shoulders with a left arm holding a staff and a right arm reaching out with an open hand, plus legs using limb IK. I'm working out how chain polylines and name arrays map to joints and spans so the spine and neck segments connect properly from the hips up through the chest to the head.

I'm defining a separate head joint under the neck tip, with a jaw joint beneath it, and assigning parent references so the spine attaches to hips, the neck attaches to the chest, and the arms attach to the chest. For the torso and rigid body parts I'm using explicit boxes/spheres/cylinders placed on bones, while limbs use smooth sweeps along the IK chains with given radii and colors, and I'm now setting up the leg chains with hip origins and foot targets.

Setting up arm chains with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints, naming the tip "handL" for the left hand, which I'll position to hold a staff positioned slightly forward-left of the body.

Settling on an elbow bend of [0,-0.5,-0.5]. Now I'm placing the staff prop as a rigid attachment to the left hand bone, running a dark rod from the floor up to about y=1.95 at x=0.38, z=0.16, with a gold ferrule spike at the bottom, and working out the crescent-shaped head geometry at the top.

Designing the staff head outline...

Now building the torso parts rigidly attached to spine joints — a dark pelvis sphere, a white armored chest bust, and teal bodysuit segments approximated with scaled spheres and cylinders rather than a full loft, to keep things simple on the bone chain.

For the coat, I'm planning extruded tabard panels hanging from the belt: a front coral panel, a white outer panel, and flaring side tails using front-view outline shapes at different z-offsets to mimic the reference's flowing coat silhouette.

I'll place the front coat panel at z=0.15 and a wider back cape panel at z=-0.12 extending down to y=0.4, flaring outward at the bottom to match the reference's wide silhouette, both rigged to the hip bone. Then I'm setting up the skull sphere skin scale and position, moving on to defining the hair next.

For the face, I'm planning simple eye geometry using small flat planes textured with eye drawings, positioned on the front of the head sphere -- I'm calculating exactly where the sphere's surface sits so the plane sits just outside it with a slight offset, adjusting the normal direction so it faces forward correctly.

Now I'm adding small dark brow rods, a tiny skin-colored nose sphere, and a coral lip sphere, then working out a gold headband using a torus shape rotated to wrap horizontally around the head -- positioning it at the right height and scaling it to match the head's curvature, plus enlarging the hair cap sphere at the back to cover more fully.

I'm checking that the hair coverage leaves the face exposed at the front while matching the skull's top height, then adding forehead fringe tufts, a ponytail bun sphere at the back, and a few spike-shaped hair tufts for texture. I'm also planning the neck as a capsule shape with a high teal-and-white collar, and starting to map the head to its corresponding skeletal bone.

Now I'm adding cyborg details: glowing cyan torus rings at the joints, gold bolt accents, a red cross decal plane on the right shoulder pauldron, and segmented plate armor with dark joint spheres on the bare arm. I'm working out the naming convention for limb bones, deciding the arm chain should be shoulder-elbow-hand and the leg chain hip-knee-ankle, with L/R suffixes for sides, so hand and foot parts attach to the correct tip joints.

Now I'm figuring out how to build the open right hand: computing a direction vector from wrist to the target point, then deriving a perpendicular "side" vector via cross product with up, so I can place five finger rods spreading outward from the palm with slight length and offset variation per finger to make them look natural.

For the fingers, I'll add joint bones per digit on the right hand (with knuckle spheres), but skip full joint rigging for the left hand since it's gripping a staff and can just use rigid capsules/rods wrapped around the pole with a fist box. I'm keeping thumbs simple and moving on to legs, where I'll sweep white armor rods over the thigh chain.

Still writing leg geometry...

Fixing the foot geometry so the bottom sits at y=0. For colors, I'll make the shin white like the boots, keeping the thigh dark to match the suit, with the hip sweep rounding smoothly where it meets the chain.

Writing arm limb sweeps...

Still working out torus scaling...

Switching to simpler elliptical cylinders for bands instead: a hip band, then building the torso from pelvis sphere, waist cylinder, and chest piece, all rigged to spine joints with specific scale and position values for each.

For the chest details, I'm adding bust spheres, a teal undersuit base, and considering how to render the V-tabard and coral stripe accent — weighing extrusions versus thin plane decals versus simple box geometry for the chest plate trim.

Adding a shoulder cap sphere and teal collar cylinder, with bust spheres protruding from the chest cylinder. For coloring, I'll make the chest cylinder white to match the jacket reference, with a teal tabard stripe and coral edge accents, keeping pauldrons white.

I'm also adding small gold ring discs on the chest and considering paint treatment—leaning toward subtle countershading rather than hard cel-shading to get a more polished, Overwatch-style surface finish for the white armor and teal accents.

For details, I'm thinking about a red cross decal on the pauldron and chevron stripe embroidery on the coat back, planning to place these as transparent plane decals in coral/teal/cream facing outward from the back panel.

Writing clip path geometry...

Now I'm also shaping the front tabard panel, extruding an outline for the white coat front skirt with a coral inner layer and a teal center strip, positioning it so it clears the thighs between the legs and covers the pelvis area.

Next I'm adding the long side coat flaps, extruding an outline along the hip at an outward offset to avoid colliding with the thigh geometry, giving the coat its flared silhouette at the sides.

I'm also placing a small glowing teal-glass canister with gold caps at the hip, positioned as a vertical cylinder near the belt to match a medical-pouch reference detail.

Now I'm planning gold trim accents on shoulders, belt buckle, and boots, aiming for roughly 150-200 total parts, and setting up a reusable helper function to simplify generating each body part with its geometry, color, bone attachment, and position.

I'm sorting out the type imports, settling on using Paint or string for the color parameter since ColorInput might not match cleanly.

Still writing helper functions...

Now I'm defining the color palette for the metal, skin, hair, and eye materials, and planning where joints and the glove for the left hand fist should attach along the arm.

Positioning fingers wrapped around the staff pole...

Working out finger positions and thumb placement...

Creating each joint with an aim toward the fingertip, parented to the chain's last joint, and double-checking that chain and limb helpers accept vector arrays as valid path input.

I'm now laying out the spine, neck, and head joints, parenting them in sequence and placing the jaw and head geometry as separate ellipsoids so the chin reads distinctly from the skull. For the arms, I'm anchoring the shoulder joints to the chest and adding a pauldron ellipsoid at the shoulder position, considering whether to add a decorative cross detail there.

Now I'm resolving the character's orientation relative to the viewer: the staff-holding arm should be on the model's right (viewer's left), matching the reference silhouette, so I'm flipping my earlier side assumptions and redefining staffSide as -1 and openSide as +1. I'm updating the hand and target coordinates accordingly for both arms, placing the canister prop on the +X hip, and reworking the elbow bend geometry for the staff arm to connect the shoulder joint to the new hand position.

With sides corrected, I'm tuning the elbow hint vectors so the staff arm bends naturally back and down while the open arm bends slightly differently, then defining the forearm's taper radii along the sweep path. I'm also positioning the pauldron's red cross emblem on the open arm's shoulder sphere, calculating the tangent plane placement and sizing so the cross decal sits flush against the curved surface without floating off the edges.

Switching approach, I decide a flat disc pauldron (cylinder scaled into a thin disc, oriented along the shoulder direction with a gold rim torus) looks better than a curved emblem on the sphere -- it gives a flush, armor-like surface for the cross decal to sit on. I'm planning the mirrored left shoulder to get a similar disc pauldron but with a plain teal face instead of the cross, then moving on to think about gold ring trim around the shoulder joints.

Now I'm working out the leg rig: hip, knee, and ankle joints positioned slightly outward for a natural stance, with limb lengths and a small bend so the chain reaches the ankle target. For the feet I'm building boots from a white box body, a gold toe-cap sphere, and a darker teal heel piece, then considering whether to add a boot shaft extending up toward the knee for a more complete look.

I'm writing a helper to compute direction vectors between points for the torus rings, then thinking about adding hair strands using spike-shaped bone elements for fringe locks.

For the ponytail, I'm sweeping a tapered path from the bun down to a tip using a curved spline with a rigid bone, and planning scattered spike tufts randomly distributed over the upper hemisphere of the head for texture.

Now I'm shifting to the staff: setting up the arm bone chain for the right hand, then building the pole as a dark rod running from near the hip up to shoulder height, with white armored sleeve rings stacked at intervals along its length near the hand grip.

Still writing staff details...

I need to adjust the blade and orb positions so they don't overlap: starting the center blade at y 2.04 and shifting the orb down to 1.98 should keep the orb visible in front without hiding the blade base.

For the side horns, I'm sketching their outline as a thick crescent shape that curves outward from the base, reaches a sharp tip, then curves back inward with a few inner contour points before closing back to the base -- checking that the edges don't cross so the smoothing won't fail on the sharp tip.

I'll skip smoothing for safety and just add a small bevel, then plan the color scheme: white horns with a teal inner layer and maybe a thin gold decorative ring. I'm also considering adding small lower wing prongs as a secondary polygon shape, plus a tilted torus geometry to serve as a halo.

For the floating plus-sign decorations, I'm building a cross-shaped extrusion outline sized small enough to avoid self-intersection, extruding it with a thin depth and cyan glow, then scattering several copies at varied positions and scales around the staff head, parented to the right hand bone.

For the eyes, I'm sketching a simple SVG with a white sclera ellipse, teal-brown iris, dark pupil, a white highlight dot, and a curved lash stroke above, leaving the skin area outside transparent.

I'm adding dark brow rods, a small skin-colored nose ellipse, coral lips, and a cyber ear piece made of a gold sphere with cyan accent positioned at the side of the head. For the cross emblem, I'm building a small SVG badge with a rounded cream background and a red plus shape centered inside.

Now I'm placing the back decal plane on the disc and working out the front tabard — extruding a teal V-shaped chest panel with coral edge trim rods running along the shoulder lines down to the waist cylinder, positioning everything to align with the chest and waist geometry already established.

I'm adding a small gold ring at the V-neck top plus a glowing cyan core disc at chest center, then sizing the belt cylinder to fit snugly within the pelvis sphere's curvature at its given height.

Next I'm placing a gold buckle with a dark/cyan inset over the belt, adding side pouches, and working out the waist and chest cylinder heights to transition smoothly into the shoulder pauldrons.

Now I'm detailing the collar and neck — a teal cylinder collar with a skin-toned capsule for the neck chain, plus a white ring piece to partially cover the neck, before shaping the trapezius with a flattened white ellipsoid at the shoulders.

I'm adding a backpack unit with teal boxes and glowing cyan slits for the cyborg look, plus a cyan neck ring accent and finger details for gripping the staff, then placing glowing cyan torus rings around the thighs positioned along the leg direction over the armor.

Working out the leg proportions now—checking that the thigh ring radius exceeds the armor radius so it reads as an overlay, and tapering the leg sweep radii from the hip down to the ankle while using a dark suit color underneath.

I'm defining countershade paint presets for the armor, teal accents, and coat panels, planning to reuse the same shading logic across many parts to keep the atlas consistent, then starting on a mottled hair paint.

Now I'm checking which imports I actually need—THREE, the builder, limb, countershade, mottle, svg, glow, rng, lerp, catmull, polyline—since unused imports will throw errors, so I need to make sure catmull is used for the ponytail curve and polyline for the spine and neck before finalizing the gold boot bands and triangle geometry.

Setting up types for the outline points, paint colors, joints, and part options so everything type-checks cleanly.

Now I'm starting the build function itself, setting up the random generator and palette, then placing the hips as the root spine joint, followed by building out the spine chain as a polyline with named segments.

Still writing leg chain...

Writing more capsule limb segments...

Still placing boot geometry... now setting the foot box at the ankle joint and adding a thin teal stripe rod running along the front of the shin.

Now I'm planning a gold torus knee ring around the pad with a glowing cyan disc inset, then moving on to mirror the same limb-building approach for both arms using the same parametric limb function.

Still building arm chains...

Working out the shoulder disc geometry and positioning for the pauldron, calculating the outward-facing decal placement using the normalized direction vector.

I'm planning two emblem designs: an open-arm cross marker for one side and a teal plus-mark for the staff side, then checking variable usage to avoid lint errors before writing the file.

Now I'm setting up small helper functions for building body parts—ellipsoids, cylinders, boxes, and torus rings—plus a lighting helper, to keep the main construction code concise.

Still working out the coat panel outline coordinates...

Adding diagonal stripe patterns and a gold cross shape to the badge, then checking that the plane's orientation and texture mirroring look correct when viewed from behind.

Working out the headband torus geometry, rotating it flat and scaling the tube cross-section anisotropically to get the right thickness and curve...

I'm sizing the headband torus so its front edge pokes just outside the hair cap while its sides stay tucked under, then placing a back bun, pigtail-like fringe ellipsoids near the temples, and a swept front lock to frame the face.
